grammar.title: The Passive: All Tenses and Passive Infinitive
grammar.explanation:
The passive is **be + past participle**. To make any tense passive, put **be** in that tense, so an approachable, chatty explanation can still sound precise.

In the present continuous, say **is being** + past participle: the room **is being decorated**. In the present perfect, say **has been** + past participle: the invitations **have been sent**.

For the future, use **will be** + past participle, and after modal verbs use modal + **be** + past participle: the form **must be signed**. Nobody who wants to bulk up should be blissfully ignorant of that modal pattern.

The passive infinitive is **to be** + past participle: she expects **to be promoted**. The passive -ing form is **being** + past participle: he hates **being interrupted**, even when he is blissfully happy.

With verbs like give and tell, the person can become the subject: **I was given** a prize. A guest who was blissfully unaware of the plan can still **be told** the truth at the door.

Use the passive to focus on the action or the thing affected, not on who did it. It is common in formal, scientific and news writing, where results **are presented** clearly and calmly.
examples: *The kitchen **is being redecorated** this week.* (present continuous passive)
*Over 200 people **have been invited** to the wedding.* (present perfect passive)
*The match **will be shown** live on TV.* (will passive)
*When we arrived, the meal **was being served**.* (past continuous passive)
*Phones **must be switched off** during the exam.* (modal passive)
*She expects **to be promoted** next year.* (passive infinitive)

practice.q: Someone is redecorating the kitchen this week. (rewrite in the passive)
practice.a: The kitchen is being redecorated this week.

practice.q: They have invited over 200 people to the wedding. (rewrite in the passive)
practice.a: Over 200 people have been invited to the wedding.

practice.q: You must switch off phones during the exam. (rewrite in the passive)

practice.q: They gave the chatty guest a warm welcome. (rewrite with the person as subject)
practice.a: The chatty guest was given a warm welcome.
